_readme: Art rules for TEMPLATE_GAME_NAME. Scaffolded empty — the first time this game needs art, FILL THIS IN before generating anything, then keep every later asset to it. These are not decoration: .github/art/build_sheet.py reads lockedPalette and enforces it on every sheet, so whatever is written here is what ships. The reason this file exists: art generated one frame at a time drifts — colours, proportions and pixel scale change between frames, and the character visibly changes identity while animating. Nothing catches that except rules applied mechanically.
_status: UNFILLED TEMPLATE — replace the descriptive fields with this game's actual look, and fill lockedPalette from the first sheet you generate.
sheetRule: NEVER generate a single frame on its own. Generate a WHOLE ROW of frames in ONE image — idle, walk, attack, left to right — because frames drawn together share proportions, palette and pixel scale by construction. A missing direction gets its own one-row image (front / side / back), never a single frame dropped into an existing set.
camera: DESCRIBE: the viewing angle every asset shares (e.g. top-down overworld, side-on platformer, three-quarter). Side views should all face the SAME direction; the game mirrors them.
style: DESCRIBE: the rendering language every asset shares — line weight, outline, how many colours, how shading works. Be explicit about what is FORBIDDEN, since that is what drifts: e.g. no dithering, no gradients, no anti-aliasing, no texture inside a colour block, no photo-realism. Enemies must use the SAME language as the hero; a finely-rendered creature next to a flat cartoon one reads as two different games.
background: SOLID FLAT PURE WHITE (#FFFFFF), completely uniform — NOT transparent. Asking the generator for transparency reliably produces a beige or gradient wash instead; build_sheet.py keys the flat white out afterwards, which works as long as the background is uniform and the subject has an outline.
framing: The whole set sits well inside the frame with a wide empty margin on all four sides — nothing touching or cut off by any edge (the bottom row is what gets clipped in practice, so say so explicitly in every prompt). Sprites must NOT overlap or touch: leave a clear gap between neighbours, or they cannot be cut apart cleanly.
paletteRule: FILL THIS IN with the hex colours of this game's first approved sheet (10-25 of them). build_sheet.py maps EVERY pixel of EVERY sheet to the nearest colour here, so once it is set, no later asset can drift into a different colour world. Add a colour only when a genuinely new material appears; never remove one that shipped art depends on.
sizeRule: Every sheet uses the same cell and the same art-pixel grid, and every sheet-based character is drawn at ONE on-screen cell size, so an art pixel is the same size for all of them. Relative size lives in the art — pass a smaller --body-height for a smaller creature — never in per-character draw sizes.
mainCharacter: DESCRIBE: species/build, silhouette, outfit, and the one or two features that must be unmistakable in EVERY frame including attacks (the feature that quietly vanishes in some frames is the usual failure).
enemies: DESCRIBE: the enemies, explicitly in the same rendering language as the main character.
frames: Per direction, in this order: idle, walk (a clearly different mid-stride pose — the code alternates it with idle), attack (a real drawn attack pose, not the idle stretched).
walkCycle: FOR A TOP-DOWN GAME WITH DIRECTIONAL WALKING (the kind the-game/Newsey is — a game with a different camera, or no walking, can ignore this): follow the RPG-Maker charset convention, because the code and the art have to agree. THREE frames per direction, and the MIDDLE frame (index 1) is a true NEUTRAL standing pose — legs together, arms relaxed — used both when idle AND as the resting beat mid-walk. Frames 0 and 2 are the two mirrored step poses. Playback while moving is [1, 0, 1, 2] on a loop, not 0->1->2, and it snaps to frame 1 the moment movement stops so nothing freezes mid-stride. Asking a generator for 'three different walking poses' yields a set with no correct idle frame — that is the classic mistake. RIGHT is never generated: it is the LEFT frames mirrored with scale(-1,1), so the LEFT row must be a TRUE SIDE PROFILE or both directions break at once. One dispatch produces the whole set: .github/workflows/generate-walksheet.yml.
constraints: No text, no labels, no numbers, no grid or graph-paper lines, no cell borders, no frames, no boxes, no drop shadows, no ground shadow, no UI, no watermarks.
pipeline:
Raw generations live in games/TEMPLATE_GAME_ID/art-src/. Turn them into a shipped sheet with the shared cutter:
  python3 .github/art/build_sheet.py --style games/TEMPLATE_GAME_ID/art-style.json --out games/TEMPLATE_GAME_ID/<name>_sheet.png --row art-src/<raw>.png [--row ...] [--blobs] [--body-height N]
It keys the background, cuts frames, scales each row by one factor, snaps to the art-pixel grid and the locked palette, and lays the frames out on a common baseline. Never hand-edit a shipped sheet — re-run the cutter.
